title: Stop Paying for File Compression — FileTools Does It Free
description: Most file compression tools either cost money or harvest your data. FileTools offers a free, private alternative that runs right in your browser.
excerpt: Free file compression without the usual catches. No sign-up, no upload limits, no data harvesting.
content:
Large files kill productivity. Email attachment limits, slow uploads, bloated storage — we all deal with it. Most people reach for whatever compression tool Google suggests first. Bad move.

The typical options: desktop software with annual subscriptions, or sketchy websites that upload your files to unknown servers. Neither is great.

## Browser-Based Compression That Actually Works

[FileTools](https://filetools.eu) takes a different approach. Your files never leave your device. The compression happens locally, inside your browser. No upload. No server processing. No privacy risk.

This matters more than people realize. That PDF with your tax returns? The contract you need to email? You probably shouldn't upload those to a random compression site.

## What You Can Compress

PDFs are the obvious use case. A 15 MB scan becomes 2 MB without visible quality loss. But [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) handles images too — JPEG, PNG, WebP. Batch processing included, so you don't compress files one at a time like it's 2005.

The interface is dead simple. Drop files in, pick your quality level, download the result. No account creation. No email harvesting popup after three uses.

## The Broader Picture

[FileTools](https://filetools.eu) isn't just compression — it's a full file conversion suite. PDF to Word, image format conversion, document merging. All free, all local.

If you're into other browser-based tools, check out [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) for AI video dubbing or [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io) for AI interior design. The trend is clear: powerful tools that respect your privacy and don't require subscriptions.

## Bottom Line

File compression shouldn't cost money in 2026. It shouldn't require trusting strangers with your documents either. [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) solves both problems. Bookmark it and move on.
